# Borderless open data lakehouse: agentic AI architecture on Google Cloud

Curated by Skill Harbor — Google's official solution skill for designing a borderless open data lakehouse: a 4-phase agent workflow. Phase 1, requirements discovery — interview the workload (data sources, metadata federation, security, analytical requirements, expected AI-agent queries) and produce a confirmed technical decomposition. Phase 2, solution design — map components to Google Cloud products using the repo's reference docs, draw a Mermaid architecture diagram (ingestion vs serving subsystems, Managed Spark as the shared ETL bridge), and compile a solution-architecture-guide.md. Phase 3, implementation plan — document prerequisites (projects, billing, APIs, IAM), generate Terraform IaC, write step-by-step deployment instructions. Phase 4, validation — dry-runs, connectivity and security checks, verification scripts, and a validation report. Covers Lakehouse for Apache Iceberg, BigQuery data agents, Cross-Cloud Interconnect, and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform across Cloud Storage, AWS S3 and Azure Blob. Honest caveats: enterprise-grade design methodology — deploying what it produces provisions real multi-cloud infrastructure, so bring a Google Cloud account with billing enabled (real cloud costs); expects the agent to fetch live Google Cloud documentation to ground its guidance; explicitly not for single-cloud warehouses. Apache-2.0 licensed. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Discovered via skills.sh.
